verdicts.reported_quantity: ART = up to 3.8% of Czech live births (2018); ART contribution to TFR rose 0.045 to 0.058, i.e. 3.1% to 3.4% of TFR; 'without ART the TFR would have stood at just 1.65 instead of 1.71 in 2020'
verdicts.note: **THE CHAPTER'S CENTRAL EXHIBIT.** It builds a TFR_nonART series by pure subtraction — B_nonART = B_total - B_ART, stated as equation (1) — and therefore treats every ART birth as counterfactually additional. It is NOT unaware of the problem: one clause concedes 'the albeit low overestimation of the number of ART births due to the possibility that some women became pregnant via sexual intercourse following ART cannot be excluded', citing refs 29-30, one of which is Osmanagaoglu's five-year follow-up of couples who DISCONTINUED ICSI. The words 'spontaneous', 'discontinued' and that author appear ZERO times in the body. **The counterfactual literature is known to the accounting literature, cited by it, characterised as 'low' without a number, and not used.** That is a sharper finding than ignorance would have been.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Among women born 1980, 81.2% of births delayed before age 30 (vs the 1968 reference cohort) would eventually be realised; in the 1974 cohort fertility recovery after 30 is COMPLETE when ART births are counted
verdicts.note: Decomposes by subtraction in as many words: 'the number of non-assisted births is obtained by subtracting the number of ART-conceived births from the number of total births'. The recuperation result is stated as conditional on counting ART births, which makes the counterfactual assumption load-bearing for the headline: complete recovery WITH ART counted is not complete recovery CAUSED by ART.

verdicts.reported_quantity: MAR contributed 3.9% of Italy's TFR in 2023; projected MAR share of births remains 4.3% under age-invariance to 2050
verdicts.note: Scenario projection to 2050. **Bears directly against v5's 'growing offset' clause: the projected share is essentially flat (3.9% to 4.3%), and the paper states population ageing alone has a negligible effect.** Assumes linear trends in mean age at childbearing and %MAR; no counterfactual is posed at all.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Czechia: ART births 3.2% of live births initially, projected 5.0% (V3) to 6.8% (V4) by 2030
verdicts.note: Projection of ART births only. Notes an ICSI-offspring sperm-concentration finding in passing, which is A.16/B.6 territory.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Ukraine: ~1.6% of children born annually via ART (from the abstract; body is Russian-language)
verdicts.note: Tag SECONDARY under Wall 8. No counterfactual posed.

verdicts.reported_quantity: US MAR share of births 1.34% (2011) to 1.97% (2019) per Vital Statistics; ART counts from SART are higher
verdicts.note: COVID as a supply interruption. Also documents that the VITAL STATISTICS and SART series disagree on the ART share — a measurement-error point the demographic-significance stage must handle before quoting any US number.

verdicts.reported_quantity: France: MAR births ascertained on >99.5% of births; US NVSS covers 96.3% of births (all states except TN and SC)
verdicts.note: Educational gradients in MAR birth prevalence, France and US. The composition result matters for arm 1: if MAR births concentrate by education, the population share and the additional share diverge.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Probability of a second live birth after a first natural vs MAR-mediated birth (Italian CedAP/SDO linkage)
verdicts.note: **The only arm-1 record in hand with a real comparison group**: it conditions on how the FIRST birth was achieved and follows parity progression. It also cites the ICSI-discontinuation literature. Parity progression conditional on conception mode is the mechanism by which ART's contribution to COMPLETED fertility differs from its contribution to first births.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Structural model of fertility recuperation limits (38pp working paper)
verdicts.note: A structural life-cycle model that does pose explicit counterfactuals ('would have still occurred in the absence of'). The counterfactuals shown in the probes are about ECONOMIC change, not ART — full extraction must check whether ART enters the model at all. If it does not, this is the ceiling on recuperation by any route and belongs in the chapter's denominator rather than its numerator.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Matched outcomes, IVF vs spontaneous pregnancies, Douala
verdicts.note: The matched design arm 1 needs. Non-OECD (tag SECONDARY under Wall 8), small, and its comparison is of pregnancy OUTCOMES rather than of birth PROBABILITY, so it bounds less than its title promises. Full extraction required before it carries weight.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Time to birth, spontaneous vs ART, among infertile groups
verdicts.note: Compares treated and untreated within an infertile population — the comparison the whole upper-bound argument rests on. **This is 1 of only 2 job-A1 records in hand out of 14.**

verdicts.reported_quantity: DiD on mandate adoption; reports ~30% of ART deliveries are multiple vs ~3% of all births
verdicts.note: Bundorf, Henne & Baker. Explicit DiD with the estimating equation printed. The multiple-birth figure is A.12's parameter appearing inside an A.17 exposure — flag both_arms_present for the A.12 handoff.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Denmark: ART associated with 4.2% of live births (2004) vs ~1.2% in the US
verdicts.note: Bitler & Schmidt. **An arm-1 quantity reported inside an arm-2 paper**, and the US/Denmark contrast is the clearest single illustration that access regimes move the ART share by a factor of three.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Australia's 2010 Medicare benefit reduction; access and government savings
verdicts.note: A DOWNWARD access shock — rarer and cleaner than an expansion, which confounds with secular demand growth.

verdicts.reported_quantity: **Israel, Maccabi, 2011-2014: IVF use among women 40-44 rose while AGE-SPECIFIC BIRTH RATES DID NOT SUBSTANTIALLY CHANGE, and live births AFTER IVF treatment DECREASED overall.**
verdicts.note: Resolves the D2 `cannot_tell`. Under unlimited publicly funded access, expanding treatment at the ages where fecundity is lowest produced no measurable movement in age-specific birth rates and a falling yield per treatment. **The single most damaging record in the frame for v5's clause**, and it is in hand.

verdicts.reported_quantity: IVF treatment SUCCESS as an instrument for childbearing; the paper explicitly examines 'the effect of IVF treatment success' as the first stage before estimating earnings effects
verdicts.note: A.12's twin-IV lesson realised. The exclusion restriction is stated as 'treatment success exclusively affects labor earnings through its first-stage impact on fertility' — so the first stage IS A.17's parameter, estimated on Danish administrative data. **Route to first-stage extraction: the magnitude is what A.17 needs and what the paper reports only in passing.**

verdicts.reported_quantity: Ontario Fertility Program (5,000 funded cycles/yr); outcome is duplicate consultations; notes inequality of access outside the GTA (0.14%)
verdicts.note: Self-describes as 'taking advantage of a natural experiment caused by a policy change'. The outcome is health-system utilisation, not births — so it establishes that the policy moved behaviour without establishing that it moved fertility.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Russia's 2014 inclusion of IVF in state insurance; DiD across differing regional arrangements. **Quotes Leridon 2004: the technology could make up for only 50% of the loss associated with postponement at ages 30-35.**
verdicts.note: Resolves the D2 `cannot_tell` to arm 2. The Leridon quotation is the recovery fraction from A.17's own anchor, restated inside an access paper — useful for showing the two arms are aware of each other even where they do not connect.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Household income gradient in help-seeking for fertility problems, representative Japanese sample
verdicts.note: Resolves to arm 2 on an income margin rather than a policy. The reduced form of the price mechanism.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Price elasticity and WTP for fertility treatment from a discrete choice experiment
verdicts.note: Arm 2's structural parameter measured directly rather than inferred from a policy. If the chapter converts any access change into a predicted birth response, this supplies the elasticity — but a stated-preference elasticity is not a revealed one, and the risk-of-bias stage must say so.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Feasibility analysis of Chinese ART insurance coverage
verdicts.note: Resolves the D2 `cannot_tell` AGAINST the cell: this is a feasibility and costing exercise, not an estimate of a birth response. A prospective policy with no outcome yet.

verdicts.reported_quantity: **65% of US workers are insured through self-insured employers exempt from state mandates under ERISA; only 41% of self-insured employers IN MANDATE STATES cover IVF, and most impose lifetime limits.**
verdicts.note: **A RISK-OF-BIAS DOMAIN FOR THE ENTIRE P1 CELL, now quantified.** Every arm-2 estimate treating 'state mandate' as the treatment is measuring a policy that fails to bind for roughly two thirds of the workforce, and covers well under half of the exempt group even where it nominally applies. The attenuation is toward zero by construction, so a small or null mandate effect is not evidence that access does not matter.

verdicts.reported_quantity: NOT RETRIEVED
verdicts.note: PLACEHOLDER — the 10-15 year return-rate study is blocked-but-open and is the decisive P5 record. Recorded here so its absence is visible in the cell's summary rather than silently missing.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Of the women who returned: six pregnancies in five women, TWO live births; 38 women reported a live birth at follow-up overall
verdicts.note: **P5's conversion problem in numbers.** The paper's own framing is that banking is 'risk management or preventive medicine because it is not certain that the women will experience' a need for it. Very small yields from thawed oocytes relative to the banking population.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Modelled effectiveness of young-age oocyte cryopreservation for extending the fertile lifespan
verdicts.note: A modelling paper, not an observed cohort. Concludes cryopreservation is 'an effective strategy' at younger ages — conditional on return, which is the parameter it does not observe.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Scoping review of fertility needs before and after freezing, split by MEDICAL and NON-MEDICAL reasons
verdicts.note: Confirms the Wall 5 taxonomy correction from the D2 assembly: the literature itself splits medical from non-medical, not oncological from elective. Conclusion is about counselling, not births.

verdicts.reported_quantity: 8-year follow-up of 892 women and 193 men after fertility assessment and counselling; adjusted OR 1.33 (95% CI 0.98-1.80) on the reported predictor; women who had conceived had on average 2.0 children
verdicts.note: **The behaviour-side P6 record, and its key adjusted estimate straddles 1.0** (CI 0.98-1.80). No other baseline predictor was found. Full extraction must establish exactly which contrast the OR refers to before the chapter cites it.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Six-year perceptions follow-up of the Danish FAC cohort
verdicts.note: Perceptions, not behaviour — the outcome is how women viewed the counselling. The Danish FAC programme supplies three horizons (2, 6, 8 years); only the 8-year paper reaches family formation.

verdicts.reported_quantity: **Austria: up to 70% of women expressing a certain, short-term intention at ages 30-32 had a child within ~4 years, but ALMOST NO WOMAN aged 42-45 did. Men fell from 60% in their 30s to 20% in their 40s.**
verdicts.note: **The cleanest statement in the frame of the gap P6 is about**: late intentions are held and not realised, and the fall is steep and age-driven. It measures the CONSEQUENCE of postponement rather than whether MAR beliefs CAUSED it — so it bounds the damage without identifying the mechanism.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Panel study of the biological clock's effect on intentions and union formation among childless people without a partner
verdicts.note: Notes selection into the childless-unpartnered subsample correlates with education — a sample-selection caution the chapter should carry.

verdicts.reported_quantity: **US: women 35+ with positive MAR views are LESS likely to forego fertility intentions (technological salience). Women in their 30s confident in MAR success are more likely to postpone — but THIS FINDING LACKS STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE. Positive MAR perceptions do NOT encourage postponement before the thirties, contradicting the paper's own hypothesis 1. MAR perceptions have a significant independent effect on intentions but 'contribute little to the overall predictive power'.**
verdicts.note: **THE DIRECT TEST OF P6's MECHANISM, and the P6 verdict should be written from it.** The authors' own summary is 'a possible but weak mediating pathway'. This converts the scope's prediction — belief measured, behaviour unmeasured — into something better: the behaviour link HAS been tested once, at the individual level, and the central estimate for the key age band is not significant. 'Measured and weak' is a stronger and more defensible verdict than 'unmeasured'.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Structural model; conclusions about the effect of an insurance policy and a medically assisted procreation programme are robust to abstracting from teenage and older mothers
verdicts.note: Journal of Economic Theory. **It models a medically assisted procreation PROGRAMME as a policy experiment** — so the theory literature has already formalised what arm 2 measures, and the chapter's mechanism section can lean on it rather than improvising.

verdicts.reported_quantity: Systematic review of worldwide ART trends 2004-2013
verdicts.note: The cross-national utilisation synthesis for stage 10.

verdicts.reported_quantity: CDC ART Surveillance, United States 2018
verdicts.note: The US exposure series, latest edition in the frame.
